messages:
Priya (Support): Hey team — Solara Systems reporting sharp p99 embed latency and occasional 500/502s since ~09:10 UTC. They say responses take 8-20s and API errors during bursts. Tenant id: solara-prod-42. Can SRE look?

Aisha (CS): cc @Diego — customer is on a Dedicated pool but not isolated. They reported this started after a config change yesterday.

Diego (SRE): Looking. Initial checks: no OOMs or node reboots, but queue length spiked on plant-gpu cluster. Suspect noisy neighbor causing queuing. Pulling request logs now.

infra-bot: Autoscaler triggered scale up for pool=plant-gpu at 2026-03-17T09:13:10Z (+2 nodes).

Diego (SRE): log snippet:
```
[09:12:58] tenant=solara-prod-42 request_id=xyz latency=18.2s queue_len=24 backend=embed-worker-7
[09:13:01] tenant=atlas-data-11 request_id=abc tokens=12000 job_type=bulk-embed queue_len=40
```
Atlas-data-11 looks like a bulk job consuming a lot of token budget and filling queues.

Ben (Oncall): Atlas-data-11 is a partner doing nightly bulk embeds. We do have a burst rule but the job uses wide parallelism so burst override kicked in. Might need stricter per-tenant concurrency caps.

Aisha (CS): Solara asked for a short-term SLA-friendly mitigation — temporary reservation or an allowlist to keep their p99 < 2s while you investigate.

Diego (SRE): Proposed mitigations:
- Short term: apply a soft per-tenant reservation on solara-prod-42 (reserve 2 slots) and tighten throttles for atlas-data-11.
- Medium: schedule tenant reshuffle so heavy batch tenants don't co-locate with latency-sensitive ones in peak windows.
- Long term: automated burst detection + automatic tenant isolation policy for pools serving mixed workloads.

Priya (Support): Customer is okay with a temporary reservation if it doesn’t require contract changes. They asked what the billing impact would be.

Aisha (CS): We’ll charge as a short-term reservation fee + metered usage. I can send a one-off billing approval.

Diego (SRE): Action plan, executing now:
1) Create a reservation:
```
POST /admin/v1/reservations
{ "tenant": "solara-prod-42", "pool": "plant-gpu", "slots": 2, "expires": "2026-03-17T12:00:00Z" }
```
2) Tighten atlas-data-11 policy:
```
PATCH /admin/v1/tenants/atlas-data-11/policy
{ "concurrency_limit": 6, "burst_limit": 2000, "priority": "low" }
```
3) Observe metrics for 10 minutes and rollback if errors increase.

infra-bot: Reservation created id=resv-98342 by diego at 2026-03-17T09:18:22Z.

Diego (SRE): Done steps 1 & 2. Early telemetry: solara p99 dropped from ~18s to ~1.9s, error rate fell to baseline. Will keep monitoring.

Priya (Support): Confirmed with Solara — latency improved and errors stopped. They asked for ETA on the reshuffle and whether this is a recurring risk.

Aisha (CS): We'll propose a reshuffle during Solara's low-traffic window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Also recommending a permanent soft-reservation during their peak hours. I'll coordinate with billing for the short fee.

Ben (Oncall): I'll add a protective circuit-breaker rule for pool=plant-gpu: if single-tenant queue_len > 50 then deprioritize or cap concurrency automatically. That should prevent a single tenant from saturating the queue.

Diego (SRE): Filed follow-up INF ticket INF-8923 to schedule reshuffle, implement autoscale safety caps, and add better per-tenant telemetry. Also attaching latency graphs and the request traces.

Priya (Support): Thanks everyone — Solara requested a brief write-up with timeframe + expected cost for the temporary reservation. I'll draft and ping legal/billing.

Aisha (CS): Good job. :thumbsup:

Ben (Oncall): Closing loop here after the post-mortem. If anything regresses, reopen with logs and tenant traces.

Priya (Support): Closing thread — marking as resolved for now.
